'''Edward Bierstone''' {{post-nominals|country=CAN|FRSC}} (born {{birth date|1946|12|21}}) is a [[Canadians|Canadian]] [[mathematician]] who specializes in [[singularity theory]], [[analytic geometry]], and differential analysis. He is [[professor emeritus]] at the [[University of Toronto Department of Mathematics|University of Toronto]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Edward Bierstone |website=[[University of Toronto Department of Mathematics|mathematics.utoronto.ca]] |url=https://www.mathematics.utoronto.ca/people/directories/all-faculty/edward-bierstone |access-date=23 August 2026}}</ref>

==Education and career==
He received his B.Sc. from the University of Toronto and his Ph.D. at [[Brandeis University]] in 1972.  He was a visiting scholar at the [[Institute for Advanced Study]] in the summer of 1973.<ref>{{cite web |website=[[Institute for Advanced Study]] |url=https://www.ias.edu/scholars/edward-bierstone |title=Edward Bierstone |access-date=23 August 2026}}</ref> He served as the Director of the [[Fields Institute]] from 2009 to 2013.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.fields.utoronto.ca/press/07-08/080629Bierstone.html |title=Edward Bierstone Appointed Next Director of Fields Institute |date=24 June 2008 |access-date=23 August 2026 |website=[[Fields Institute]]}}</ref>

==Recognition==
Bierstone was elected a member of the [[Royal Society of Canada]] in 1992 and, together with [[Pierre Milman]], received the [[Jeffery–Williams Prize]] in 2005. In 2012, he became a fellow of the [[American Mathematical Society]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.ams.org/profession/fellows-list |title=List of Fellows of the American Mathematical Society |access-date=23 August 2026}}</ref> In 2018, the [[Canadian Mathematical Society]] listed him in their inaugural class of fellows.<ref>{{citation|url=https://cms.math.ca/MediaReleases/2018/Fellows|title=Canadian Mathematical Society Inaugural Class of Fellows|publisher=Canadian Mathematical Society|date=December 7, 2018|access-date=January 7, 2020|archive-date=January 22, 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210122125232/https://www2.cms.math.ca/MediaReleases/2018/Fellows|url-status=dead}}</ref>
